model:
Alphabet business-model profile (AI compute lens), 29 October 2026. Sources: FY25 10-K, 3Q26 8-K Ex. 99.1 and 10-Q, 3Q26 call.

1. Engine: Alphabet turns Search and YouTube ad cash flow plus Aa2/AA+ debt and some equity into TPUs, GPUs, data centers and power, and monetizes that compute through Google Cloud (GCP consumption, AI infrastructure, TPU systems sold into customer and partner data centers), Gemini, and its own products.

2. Revenue map: Cloud revenue = deployed capacity x utilization x price per unit of compute, plus TPU system product sales recognized on delivery (first in 2Q26, ramp in 2027). Cloud backlog $560.8bn at 30 Sep 2026 (just over 55% within 24 months), incl. $16.8bn with Crux AI (related party). Search & other $63.35bn in 3Q26 (+12%).

3. Costs: depreciation $8.37bn in 3Q26 (+49% YoY); servers and network about 65% of technical infrastructure capex, 6-year lives; data centers 7 to 40 years. TPU hardware inventory flows through cost of revenues. Third-party bridging capacity (short-term lease about $6.0bn) from end-3Q26. Energy take-or-pay contracts.

4. Capital and funding: capex $132.0bn in 9M26, FY26 guide $195bn to $205bn, 2027 'increase significantly'. Funded by OCF ($179.6bn TTM), senior unsecured notes (face $127.5bn; 3Q26 dollar notes 5.55% weighted coupon), common equity and 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred (2026), ATM ($27.6bn left). Off balance sheet: leases not yet commenced $130.5bn, data center backstops $75.7bn ($48.0bn executed as credit derivatives, terms up to 15 years, right to take over leases), financial guarantees $22.8bn (energy equipment $16.2bn, TPU repurchase $6.6bn), purchase commitments $924.4bn.

5. Sensitivities: Search monetization of AI Mode; Cloud capacity timing and rented-capacity cost; TPU pricing and resale values; rates and credit spreads; power availability; equity marks on SpaceX and private stakes (EPS only).

6. Competitive position: only hyperscaler with its own chips, frontier models and cloud at scale; about 100 TPU customers; TPU distribution via Oracle and Crux AI (Blackstone JV). Competitors: Microsoft/OpenAI, Amazon/Anthropic (shared), Nvidia-based neoclouds.

7. What would break it: Search growth falling to low single digits while capex rises; TPU demand concentrated in a few labs that falter; backstops called at scale; a funding market that stops absorbing hyperscaler debt at AA spreads; rented capacity becoming permanent and diluting Cloud margins.
name: Alphabet
